example:
In a shallow clone with no history beyond the last commit, each window holds
only the files' contents on disk and in that commit. `habeas status` says that
coverage history is incomplete and warns about items those contents do not
cover. {test}`requirements.references.coverage.history`
rationale:
The example's scenario is a depth-1 shallow clone. In it, `habeas status` should say coverage history is incomplete and warn about items that the on-disk contents and the last commit do not cover. Four tests in `tests/coverage.rs` carry a {test} reference to the example, and two of them cover the full scenario. I read only the tests and their helpers, not the library code, so the judgment rests on the tests' assertions.

- **Setup.** `a_shallow_clone_uses_the_history_it_has_and_says_so` and `status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete` both build a project with two commits. The first commit's record reads `fn[parse]`, and the last commit's record reads nothing. Each then runs `git clone --depth 1 file://…`, so the clone has only the last commit.
- **Incomplete history is reported.** `a_shallow_clone_uses_the_history_it_has_and_says_so` asserts `coverage_warnings(&target).incomplete`. `status_shows_coverage_warnings_and_says_when_history_is_incomplete` asserts that `status_markdown` output contains "Coverage history is incomplete". The same test first checks that the unshallow repository's status does not say "history is incomplete".
- **Warnings use only the available contents.** In the first test, `warned(&target)` equals `["parse", "render", "helper"]`. That is correct because the only commit available no longer reads `parse`. The full repository warns only about `["render", "helper"]`, so the shallow window is shown to be narrower than the full history. The status test also asserts that the status output contains "function parse has no recent coverage".
- **Supporting tests.** `incomplete_history_is_noted_even_with_nothing_to_warn_about` asserts that a shallow clone with no warnings still reports `incomplete: true` and the status note. `a_shallow_clone_holding_every_window_is_complete` asserts that a clone reaching the commit before the record was added is not marked incomplete, while one that stops at the commit adding it is.

The tests reach `habeas status` through the library functions `status_markdown` and `coverage_warnings`, not by running the binary. Together they assert each expected outcome in the example.

:::{req} coverage.history
An item has recent coverage when it has a reference that covers it under
{cite}`requirements.references.rust_item_coverage`, or when its outline node, or
an outline node containing it, is named by file and selector in the inputs of
any version of an existing evidence record, citation review, or site review in
its coverage window. A file's coverage window MUST be its current contents on
disk, committed or not, together with its contents in each of the last N
commits in its Git history that changed it, read through a Git library rather
than by running `git`. A recorded hash MUST NOT matter here: an earlier version
names the node, whatever its code was then. N MUST be the workspace
`[coverage]` setting `reauthorings`, a positive integer, and 3 when it is not
set. When the history is unavailable, such as outside Git or in a shallow clone
missing those commits, the window MUST be the commits that are available, and
the commands of {cite}`requirements.references.coverage.report` MUST say that
coverage history is incomplete.
